liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (4 reviews): Played up-tempo, with Jerry strong throughout; Reviewer especially liked this version [16][18][23][26]
- **Playin' in the Band** (4 reviews): The Playin' > Uncle John's > Playin' sequence was a highlight for this listener; It had a tropical sound [21][24][26][27]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (2 reviews): Fast tempo, tight band, with strong harmony singing; Singled out as an especially sweet Jerry number [16][25]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): A short jam inside the opener got the night started [16]
- **Just A Little Light** (1 review): Brent sang it strongly, with Jerry's bent-note solos throughout [18]
- **Cold Rain & Snow** (1 review): Vocals were top notch, coming right after Memphis Blues [19]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Features amazing guitar work from Jerry [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-10-25 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd89-10-25 s1t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd89-10-25 s1t03 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd89-10-25 s1t04 Just A Little Light**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd89-10-25 s1t05 Friend Of The Devil**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd89-10-25 s1t06 Stuck Inside Of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd89-10-25 s1t07 Cold Rain & Snow**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd89-10-25 s1t08 Picasso Moon**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-10-25.142606.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 175 min [1]
- **gd89-10-25.sbd.sacks.1828.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 171 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1989-10-25.143033.sbd.miller.fixed.flac2496**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 173 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1989-10-25.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83398.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 173 min; rated 2.2/5 by 5 [5]. Said about its sound: This 1989 soundboard mix has loud vocals and hi-hat, with everything else muddy in the background; Reviewer says this soundboard source sounds great [22][27]

## Around the show

- Florida had few Dead shows until around this time, then got quite a few for some years [21]
- Treated as a warm-up for the following night, which the reviewer rated higher for playing [18]
- Gets overlooked because of the following night's show [19]
- Reviewer finds it weaker than Dick's Picks 33 [23]
- Seen as the calm before the storm of the second night [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-10-25.142606.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master (FOB)Audience Dat; Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics @ 110 degrees, ORTF, Schoeps t-bar, hand held, chin high > Monster… [1]
- **gd89-10-25.sbd.sacks.1828.sbeok.shnf**: source: Cassette SBD> DATs> CDRs> EAC> SHN [2]. Also: Cassette soundboard to DATs to CDRs, then EAC to SHN, via Peter L., Sean Cribbs and Darrin Sacks [2]
- **gd1989-10-25.143033.sbd.miller.fixed.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [3]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined for completeness, and this source has a fixed Hell In A Bucket [3]
- **gd1989-10-25.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83398.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [5]. Also: Nakamichi 300/CP4 cassette master transferred with Tascam HD-P2; tapes from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker, patch from Bill Tetzeli [5]
